texts: On day 190 of Year 1, Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown.
The mist-light attracted a handful of nightmoths.
Coraline Ash counted four nightmoths at the lantern at the third watch.
The nightmoths landed on the lantern.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lantern.
Coraline Ash collected a small heap of silken threads from the lantern at dawn on day 191 of Year 1.
Coraline Ash carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the first cauldron on day 191 of Year 1.
Mire-essence formed in the first cauldron by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in a clay vessel.
Coraline Ash drew the stored mire-essence at sundown on day 191 of Year 1.

q1_issues.issue: (Ordinal sk_cauldron_1 1 cauldron) fills Ordinal's scale slot with the entity's own class, but the prompt defines that slot as an ordering scale — the associated event or an explicit "-est" dimension — neither of which "the first cauldron" supplies.

"left silken threads on the lantern" gives the threads Patient, but the threads are deposited rather than created, destroyed, consumed or physically changed; the prompt's explicit tie-breaker ("when the test is unclear, default to Theme") points to Theme, and the same role is copied into the distribution rule at index 51.

q2_gaps: an enumerative / identifying ordinal on an object ("the first cauldron") — Ordinal is defined as rank on an ordering scale (an event, or an "-est" dimension), and the instruction set licenses no filler for a bare positional label among like objects

"day 190 / day 191 of Year 1" — a day-of-year index; the (Day <n>) term is defined and exemplified as the day within a stated month, so a day count with no month has no distinct term (and cannot feed the seeded same-year-month day ordering)
review.notes: Parallel bare-mass objects are handled inconsistently — "burned mire-essence" takes the bare kind constant while "produced mist-light" mints sk_mist_light_1 (the witness is what lets the next sentence's definite "the mist-light" corefer, so the inconsistency is in the first clause). The compound handling is otherwise exact: silken_thread with both genus and the material-adjective modifier, clay_vessel and nightmoth and sea_water with genus only.

issues.reason: The gap half stands — Ordinal's <scale> is defined as the associated ordering event or an explicit "-est" dimension and "the first cauldron" supplies neither — but the defect half does not, because (Ordinal sk_cauldron_1 1 cauldron) states nothing false (this is the first among the cauldrons), uses a licensed head, and Core patterns forbids silently dropping the stated restrictive "first", so it is exactly the graceful improvisation the calibration line protects.

"Left silken threads on the lantern" deposits the threads without creating, destroying, consuming or physically changing them, so the prompt's one yes/no object test yields Theme (the "moved / swapped → Theme, the object is displaced not altered" branch), and the explicit "when the test is unclear, default to Theme" tiebreaker points the same way.

gaps_confirmed: Enumerative / identifying ordinal on an object ("the first cauldron"): Ordinal's <scale> slot has no licensed filler — no associated ordering event, no "-est" dimension, and the reserved `unspecified` symbol is licensed only in Measure-family slots.

Day-of-year index ("day 190 / day 191 of Year 1"): (Day <n>) is defined and exemplified as the day within a stated month, so a monthless day count has no distinct granularity term and cannot feed the seeded same-year-month day ordering.
new_gaps: Numbered recurring time period ("at the third watch"): neither the calendar terms (Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute), the day-part constants, nor Ordinal covers it, so the rank survives only buried inside an opaque constant (third_watch) and cannot be queried or ordered; a licensed form would need a term carrying both the period kind and its index.

Stacked "in" PPs where the inner names a medium rather than a place ("boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the first cauldron"): the stacked-place rule is written for a second "in <Place>" on a place NP, and a bare mass kind cannot go in LocatedIn's entity slot, so nothing licenses containing the medium in the vessel and the parse emits two co-equal Location atoms on one boiling event.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form for the confirmed issue is (Theme sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1) in place of the Patient atom, with the same Theme role in the s7_dist_rule conclusion's per-member leave event — leaving deposits the threads unchanged, which is the displacement branch of the change test, and the role is licensed and available, so this defect has a fix and files no new gap.
adjudication.notes: The reviewer's note is right that mire-essence is a bare kind constant in s2 but a witness sk_mire_essence_1 in s11 for what the passage treats as one substance, though neither choice is itself unlicensed — the s2 bare-kind object is the non-specific reading the prompt reserves the class symbol for. The rest of the compound handling checks out exactly: silken_thread with genus plus the material-adjective modifier, clay_vessel / nightmoth / sea_water / mist_light with genus only (noun modifiers correctly unexposed).
